title: Quality signal synthesis brief: onboarding pulse and short-term mitigations
content:
Executive summary:

This brief is a compact pulse on the most recent onboarding evals and the signal we are seeing in weekly quality telemetry. It synthesizes the top failure modes discovered across new-model promptsets (March 28 -> April 19 window), the immediate mitigations we recommend for production-facing routes, and a prioritized set of follow-ups for the next two sprints. This is intentionally terse — the goal is rapid alignment and owner assignment.

Top-line metrics (coarse):
- Onboarded model cohort: 7 candidates tested across 18 promptsets.
- Baseline pass-rate (pre-onboard baseline median): 91.2%
- Current median pass-rate across promptsets: 86.7% (delta -4.5pp)
- Hallucination/unsupported-fact flags: +2.5x relative to baseline for retrieval-heavy promptsets
- Time-to-detect (median signal latency in our dashboards): ~26 hours (improving, target <24h)

Why this matters now:
- Two customers (enterprise-D, fintech-P) reported intermittent numeric-precision errors in billing-related prompts; the error class maps to our "numeric-truncation" cluster and shows up in live telemetry at low volume but high-severity.
- We are seeing drifting tokenization edge-cases on long-context prompts (sequence >2.5k tokens) that previously passed on the prod model. These are latent regressions that will worsen with larger promptsets.

Notable failure clusters (ranked by combined severity * frequency):
1) Numeric truncation / rounding drift
   - Symptoms: last-digit loss in 10x scale numbers, currency formatting mistakes, off-by-one totals in short arithmetic reasoning.
   - Prompts affected: billing-qA-v1, invoice-summarizer-v2, spend-aggregation-tests
   - Immediate risk: high for finance flows; low-volume but customer-impacting.

2) Entity hallucination in retrieval contexts
   - Symptoms: confidently asserted facts not present in retrieved snippets (especially with fuzzy match hits).
   - Prompts affected: kb-retrieval-v3, support-chat-kb-extracts
   - Observed pattern: model favors high-recall phrasing that synthesizes plausible but incorrect names when retrieval score <0.45.

3) Context window truncation for long prompts
   - Symptoms: abrupt topic switches, missing critical instructions, fallback to generic answers when the tail of a prompt is clipped.
   - Prompts affected: long-ticket-history-qa, user-session-chronicle

4) Formatting regression for structured outputs
   - Symptoms: malformed JSON output (extra commas, missing keys), inconsistent date formats breaking downstream parsers.
   - Prompts affected: structured-response-v1, data-table-extracts

Promptset gaps discovered (quick notes):
- Few prompts exercise boundary rounding behaviour for currencies and percentages; we should expand prompt coverage for edge-digit arithmetic and locale-specific currency formats.
- Retrieval tests lack adversarial negatives where the KB contains similar-but-wrong records; add synthetic near-miss entries into test KB for robust discrimination.
- Long-context test corpus is biased towards English-only transcripts; need multilingual long-context samples to catch tokenization drift with multi-byte characters.

Diagnostics run this week (high-level):
- Bulk diff against prod model on 1k ticket-simulated prompts (seeded replay): flagged 78 prompts with semantic divergence; triaged to numeric (34), retrieval (28), formatting (16).
- Tokenizer drift spot-check: compared token counts on 500 long prompts between candidate and baseline models — 12% had >=1 token difference affecting KV-cache alignment.
- Canary traffic A/B: routed 1% of dedicated-customer traffic to candidate variant; observed 3 customer-facing errors (numeric) — paused ramp for billing routes.

Short-term mitigations (apply in next 72 hours):
- Deployment guardrail: add explicit canary gating on routes tagged "finance/*" and "billing/*". Action: Maya Chen. Linear: RED-1345.
- Prompt-level hard-stop: for structured outputs, add output schema validation & automatic fallback to baseline model on schema violation (2x attempts then baseline). Action: Diego Alvarez.
- Increase alert sensitivity for numeric-delta signals (lower threshold to capture off-by-one anomalies) for the next 7 days. Action: Ravi Patel.

Medium-term actions (2 sprints):
- Promptset augmentation: add 350 synthetic numeric-edge prompts and 200 retrieval near-miss cases to the onboarding suite. Owner: Asha Mehta. Blocker: generation scripts (GH PR #412).
- Tokenizer and KV-cache audit: run end-to-end tokenization parity tests and KV alignment check on large-batch replay harness; expected effort 3 dev-days. Owner: Platform infra lead (assigned: Priya Rao).
- Structured-output regression test harness: implement fuzzing for JSON schema outputs with random unicode payloads. Owner: QA automation.

Low-effort experiments to run this sprint (to validate hypotheses):
- Soft-constrain generation temperature on finance routes (0.0 -> 0.2 sweep) and log differences. Hypothesis: lower temp reduces hallucination rate for numeric answers. Owner: Diego.
- Retrieval score threshold bump: increase strictness to 0.5 for KB route and compare precision/recall curve. Owner: Maya.

Risks and open questions: 
- Will strict retrieval thresholds materially reduce user-perceived recall? We need a customer impact trial.
- Is the tokenizer drift caused by recent tokenization-related optimization in the runtime or by model tokenizer changes? Requires JVM/runtime trace and tokenizer config diff.
- Are any of the numeric regressions introduced by quantization/FP16 kernel changes? Need coordinated infra + applied-ML repro.

Action item register (quick table):
- RED-1345: add billing route canary gating and emergency rollback hook (Maya Chen) — due 2026-04-23
- GH#412: promptset augmentation scripts and seed generation (Asha Mehta) — due 2026-04-29
- Create KV-cache parity job and schedule nightly (Priya Rao) — due 2026-04-30
- Implement structured-output schema fallback (Diego Alvarez) — due 2026-04-25
- Alert threshold tuning and dashboard tile for numeric-delta (Ravi Patel) — due 2026-04-23

Notes to self / rough thoughts: 
- Consider adding a small deterministic test harness (single-seed decoding with grammar checks) for money/currency prompts — cheap and high value for finance customers.
- If tokenizer delta persists after parity job, escalate to serving-runtime for kernel/embedding alignment check.

Supporting logs & where to look quickly: 
- Regression diff artifacts: gs://redwood-onboard/regressions/2026-04-19/diffs.tar.gz
- Dashboard (internal): https://console.redwood/ops/onboard/signal-summary?range=2w
- Slack thread (designated): #onboard-signals (pinned messages: RED-1345 brief)

Next sync: short standup Tuesday 2026-04-22 10:30am PT to triage early canary feedback; full review on 2026-04-27 with results from augmentations and parity runs.

Appendix (brief raw examples):
- Example failing prompt (numeric truncation): "Summarize total charges for account 452399: charges are [10000, 0, 0, 0, 1]." Candidate model returned total 1000 instead of 10001.
- Example retrieval hallucination case: user asks for policy X; model asserts policy author name not present in retrieved snippet (false positive).

If you want a condensed 1-pager or a slide deck version for Eng-Weekly, I can spin one out from this note — ping me.

-- Asha
